candidate.blueprint_locator: Basic Care and Comfort — mobility, positioning and safe use of assistive devices
candidate.educational_objective: Select safe patient-handling equipment that accommodates the client's size, weight, and mobility needs without exceeding equipment limits.

options.A: Select assistive equipment that is appropriate for the client's size, weight, mobility needs, and the device's safe-use limits.
options.B: Use standard equipment even when the client's weight exceeds its safe capacity.
options.C: Avoid assistive equipment so the client is not embarrassed.
options.D: Assume every hospital bed, lift, and chair is safe for clients of any weight.

candidate.rationale: NIOSH safe-patient-handling guidance recommends using assistive lifting technology and matching handling methods to patient needs. NIOSH has specifically defined bariatric handling challenges in relation to patients whose size or weight can exceed standard equipment capacity. Equipment should therefore be selected and used within its safe limits rather than overloaded. Therefore A is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Safe-patient-handling programs use assistive equipment matched to handling needs; higher patient weight/size can exceed standard equipment capacity, requiring appropriate equipment rather than unsafe overloading.
candidate.source_document_title: About Safe Patient Handling and Mobility; Preventing Back Injuries in Health Care Settings
candidate.source_locator: SPHM — use assistive lifting devices and prevention solutions; bariatric handling — patient size/weight may exceed standard equipment safety capacity
candidate.source_organization: CDC / National Institute for Occupational Safety and Health (NIOSH)
candidate.source_version_date: SPHM page May 9, 2024; bariatric handling background retained in NIOSH safety guidance
candidate.stem: A client requires assistance with mobility and has a body size that exceeds the safe capacity of some standard patient-handling equipment. Which action is appropriate?
